summary: The C10 is Stellantis-distributed Leapmotor's mid-size electric SUV, sold in Australia as a value play against the Tesla Model Y and Kia EV5; since the June 2026 update the battery-electric range is down to two grades, the $49,888 Design LR and the $53,888 AWD Sports+ Special Edition, after the entry 69.9kWh Style was dropped. Australian reviewers broadly agree on the package — RACV, CarExpert and CarsGuide all praise its limousine-like rear legroom, comfortable ride and equipment level, and CarsGuide's 2026 BEV Design review scored it 7.5/10 after an over-the-air update tamed the intrusive driver-assist alerts. Where they diverge is how much the usability faults matter: the missing Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, everything-in-the-touchscreen layout and fiddly key card drew consistent criticism, Chasing Cars marked the related range-extender C10 down to 5.5/10 for grabby brakes and numb steering, and RACV warned buyers about brand risk given Leapmotor's tiny local volume.
pros: The $49,888 Design LR undercuts a Kia EV5 Air Long Range by about $11,000 and a BYD Sealion 7 Premium by about $5,000, with a panoramic roof, 14.6-inch screen and a full driver-assist suite standard
Class-leading rear legroom on a flat floor — reviewers consistently rate the second row as the C10's standout, ahead of the Model Y and EV5
The Design LR's 81.9kWh usable LFP battery, 800V architecture and 180kW DC charging (30-80% in about 22 minutes) give 510km WLTP for the same price the 69.9kWh Design used to cost
The AWD Sports+ Special Edition brings 440kW and a claimed 4.0-second 0-100km/h for $53,888 before on-roads, Model Y Performance pace for far less money
Rated to tow 1500kg braked, double the BYD Sealion 7 RWD's 750kg, with an eight-year/160,000km battery warranty and a five-star ANCAP rating from 2024 testing
cons: No Apple CarPlay or Android Auto on any grade, with mirrors, vents and most functions buried in the touchscreen and no physical console buttons
The quoted 581L boot is measured to the roof; to the cargo cover it is about 435L, behind the Sealion 7's 500L and EV5's 513L
Leapmotor cut the C10's warranty from seven years/160,000km to six years/150,000km for MY25, so it now trails the seven years offered by Kia, MG, Deepal and Geely

Weak resale outlook: Leapmotor's local volume is tiny, the BEV line-up has been cut to two grades (the AWD Sports+ was limited to 50 cars), and the brand leans on recurring cashback and $0 on-road campaigns to move stock
Numb steering, grabby friction brakes that are hard to modulate in traffic, and a plastic key card held against the mirror to unlock that CarsGuide called weird
